title: Why this shape?
author: Kenneth Hill

whatThisIs: The Mountain arranges the whole Bible into 11 stages -- Genesis 1 through Revelation 22 -- climbing toward the Gospels and then descending, with each stage on the way up paired with one on the way down (Creation with the New Creation, the Flood with the Final Judgment, and so on).

That arrangement is a reading lens this app offers, not a claim the Bible itself makes about its own structure. Scripture nowhere says it is organized into eleven stages, or that these particular passages mirror each other. The pairing is an editorial judgment -- a way of noticing real, citable parallels between passages (shared images, shared vocabulary, a judgment-then-restoration pattern) and arranging the canon around them so they're easier to compare side by side.
author_statement: This lens was built by Kenneth Hill, this app's author, for this app. It is not attributed to, or endorsed by, any named scholar, tradition, or published work.
method: The method is a traditional one, sometimes called a chiastic or ascent/descent reading of the canon: pair the first things with the last things (Eden with the New Jerusalem), the judgment-of-the-world passages with each other (the Flood with Revelation's judgments), the empire passages with each other (Babel with Babylon), and the covenant-people passages with each other (Israel with the Church) -- with the Gospels, where this lens places the person of Jesus Christ, as the structural turning point between the two halves.

This app does not have a documented citation for where this specific eleven-stage grouping and these specific chapter boundaries came from. It is Kenneth Hill's own curated arrangement, built for this app. If you are looking for the scholarly lineage of chiastic/ascent-descent readings of the Bible's shape generally, that is a real and old interpretive tradition -- but no specific source for THIS app's eleven stages is recorded anywhere in this project's own documents, and this screen will not pretend one exists. If that changes, this paragraph should be the first thing updated.
cautions: The Genesis 3-5 / Revelation 20 pairing: Genesis 3 narrates a serpent, not a figure the text names "Satan." That identification is made later in the canon (Revelation 12:9, 20:2). This app's own Genesis 3 lesson keeps that distinction in its Context section; this lens's stage titles have been rephrased to keep it too (see the Genesis 3-5 stage).

The Israel / Church pairing (Genesis 12-Malachi with Acts-Jude): how the Church relates to Israel -- continuity, discontinuity, something else -- is a question Christian traditions answer differently (see Romans 9-11), and this lens deliberately does not adjudicate it. Pairing the two stages for comparison is not this app asserting an answer.
